questions.question: Wheatstone bridge is an arrangement of _____ resistors used for accurate measurement of resistance.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**four.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Wheatstone bridge, also known as the** resistance bridge,** calculates the unknown resistance by balancing two legs of the ground circuit.
 
• One leg includes the element of unknown resistance.
 
• The Wheatstone Bridge Circuit comprises two known resistors, one unknown resistor, and one variable resistor connected in the form of ground.
 
• This ground is veritably dependable as it gives accurate measures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Wheatstone Bridge Principal:**

 
 
• The Wheatstone bridge works on the principle of null deflection, i.e. the rate of their resistances is equal, and no current flows through the circuit.
 
• Under normal conditions, the ground is in an unstable condition where current overflows through the galvanometer.
 
• The bridge is said to be balanced when no current flows through the galvanometer.
 
• This condition can be achieved by conforming the known resistance and variable resistance.
 
 
 
• **Wheatstone Bridge Formula:**
 
 
• Following is the formula used for the Wheatstone bridge:
 
• R = PS/Q
 
• Where, **R is the unknown resistance**
 
• **S is the standard arm of the bridge**
 
• **P and Q is the ratio of the arm of the bridge**

questions.question: Select the name of the hydrocarbon with a structural formula CH₃ – CH₂ – CH₂ – CH₂ – CH₂– CH₃.

• **n-Hexane** is the name of the hydrocarbon with the structural formula CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃.
 
• It is a straight-chain alkane with six carbon atoms.
 
• The prefix "n-" denotes a normal or unbranched chain structure.
 
• n-Hexane is commonly used in laboratories and industry as a non-polar solvent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Hexane is also used in the extraction of edible oils from seeds and vegetables.
 
• Its chemical formula is C₆H₁₄, and it is part of the alkane series of hydrocarbons.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT belong to the family of organic compounds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Ammonia__**.

__
 
• **Organic compounds:-**

 
 
• These are typically composed of carbon and hydrogen atoms, and they may also contain other elements such as oxygen, nitrogen, sulfur, and phosphorus.
 
• Ammonia is a simple inorganic compound that contains only nitrogen and hydrogen atoms.
 
• It does not have a carbon skeleton, which is a defining characteristic of organic compounds.
 
• **Ammonia (NH3) is not an organic compound.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nonane:-**

 
 
• It is an alkane, which is a type of hydrocarbon that has only single bonds between its carbon atoms.
 
• It is a colorless, flammable liquid with a mild odor.
 
• Nonane is used in a variety of applications, including as a fuel, a solvent, and a component of gasoline.
 
 
 
• **Furan:-**
 
 
• It is an organic compound with the formula C₄H₄O.
 
• It is a colorless, volatile liquid with a sweet, burnt-sugar odor. Furan is found in a variety of foods, including coffee, tea, and roasted nuts.
 
• It is also used in the production of plastics and pharmaceuticals.
 
 
 
• **Decane:-**
 
 
• It is an alkane with the formula C₁₀H₂₂.
 
• It is a colorless, flammable liquid with a mild odor. Decane is used in a variety of applications, including as a fuel, a solvent, and a component of gasoline.

questions.question: Which of the following types of elements is included in the leftmost group of the periodic table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alkali metals.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**__**Alkali metals:**__

__
 
• **Alkali metals belong to the s-block elements** occupying the **leftmost side** of the periodic table.
 
• Alkali metals** readily lose electrons**, making them ;the most reactive elements on earth.
 
• In general ‘alkali’ refers to the **basic or alkaline nature** of their metal hydroxides.
 
• The compounds are called alkali metals because when they **react with water** they** usually form alkalies which are strong bases** that can easily neutralize the strong acids.
 
• Alkali metals have an outer electronic configuration (ns1).
 
• They occupy the** first column of the periodic table.**
 
• Alkali elements are **Lithium(Li), Sodium(Na), Potassium (K), Rubidium (Ru), Cesium (Cs) and Francium (Fr)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Our periodic table is given by **Moseley **and has in total** 7 periods running horizontally and 18 groups running vertically.**
 
• They are also further divided into **s, p, d, and f blocks** depending on the placement of the outermost electrons.
 
• Elements belonging to the same blocks resemble their chemical and physical properties.
 
 
• The **s block elements** lie in the 1st and 2nd groups.
 
• The** p block elements** belong to groups 13-18.
 
• The** d and f block elements** lie in the middle from group number 3-12.

questions.question: Which of the following is a severe form of malnutrition that commonly affects infants and toddlers, most often around the age of weaning through age 5?

__
 
• ​**Kwashiorkor **is a form of** malnutrition distinguished** by a significant **lack of protein.**
 
• It results in **abdominal swelling and fluid retention.**
 
• **Kwashiorkor most frequently impacts children**.
 
• It is more prevalent in** developing nations** with** high levels of poverty and food insecurity.**
 
• Kwashiorkor patients may have** enough food to eat,** but not **enough protein.**
 
• Kwashiorkor can be corrected by **eating more protein** and more **calories** overall.

questions.question: How big are red blood cells in diameter?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7.5 µm**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Red blood cells, or erythrocytes,** are **minuscule in size**, requiring a microscope for visibility.
 
• Measuring around **7.5 micrometers in diameter,** they are vital for **transporting oxygen** throughout the body.
 
• Each red blood cell **contains hemoglobin,** a pigment that binds to oxygen and imparts the cells with their characteristic red color.
 
• Their unique biconcave disc shape provides increased surface area and flexibility.
 
• Despite their crucial role, red blood cells have a relatively short lifespan of approximately 120 days.
 
• After this period, they are eliminated from circulation by the spleen and liver.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **White blood cells**, also known as leukocytes, are essential for defending the body against infections.
 
• Despite their small size, they possess a distinct nucleus.
 
• Constituting only about 1% of blood volume, they are outnumbered by red blood cells.
 
• White blood cells originate in the bone marrow, a soft tissue located within bones.

questions.question: Which thin flexible barrier separates the internal environment of the cell from the extracellular fluid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plasma membrane.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The plasma membrane is selectively permeable because hydrophobic molecules and small polar molecules can diffuse through the lipid layer, but ions and large polar molecules cannot. 
 
• Integral membrane proteins enable ions and large polar molecules to pass through the membrane by passive or active transport.
 
• Selectively permeable means a membrane allows the passage of some molecules or ions and inhibits the passage of others.
 
• The capacity to filter molecular transport in this manner is called selective permeability. This is also called differential permeability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0c96da9b13f2ad86d8f363702005a8221c34d877ec17bae0442afd43fdc5e6ea.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Other types of membranes on the basis of permeability:

 
 
• Impermeable membrane: Substances of any type can not pass through them.
 
• Permeable membranes: Substances of any type can pass through them.
 
• Semi-permeable membrane: These are the membrane which permits the movement of only solvent molecules through them.

questions.question: Which formula is used to represent the three-dimensional structures of molecules using a two-dimensional surface like a sheet of paper or a computer screen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Dash-wedge formula.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The wedge and dash notation is used to represent three-dimensional structures of molecules using a two-dimensional surface, like a sheet of paper or a computer screen.
 
• This type of structure is also called **wedge-dash notation or wedges-and-dash notation.**
 
• It is commonly used in organic chemistry, though you may see it any time a molecule structure is given.
 
• **Wedges –** Solid triangular wedges represent chemical bonds and groups that are coming out of the page, toward you.
 
• **Dashes –** Dashed triangular shapes represent chemical bonds and groups extending back behind the page.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bond Line Formula:**

 
 
• A bond line structural formula is another way of structural representation of organic compounds.
 
• Here, every bond is represented as a line in a zigzag manner.
 
• If not specified, every terminal is assumed to be a **methyl (-CH3) group.**
 
 
 
• **Lewis structure formula :**
 
 
• The Lewis structure, also known as an electron fleck structure, is a diagrammatic representation of determining the total number of valence electrons present in a snippet that are ready to form bonds to form a patch and, ultimately, an emulsion.
 
 
 
• **Condensed structural formula:**
 
 
• In the condensed structural formula, every carbon atom is represented individually, and the following carbon atoms are placed to the atoms that are bonded to that particular carbon atom.

questions.question: Which of the following algae is also called kelp and found in the deep sea?

• Laminaria are known for their large, leafy blades and their ability to withstand harsh conditions.
 
• They are an important food source for marine invertebrates and are also used as a fertilizer, a source of alginates, and a dietary supplement.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct?

I. When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called radial symmetry.

II. Where the body can be divided into identical left and right halves in only one plane, exhibit bilateral symmetry.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Body Symmetry:

 
 
• There are 3 types of symmetry: Bilateral, Radial, and Asymmetrical.
 
• Bilateral Symmetry:
 
 
• Animals, whose bodies can be **divided into left and right halves**, are said to be bilaterally symmetrical.
 
• For example Platyhelminthes, Annelida, Arthropoda, Chordata, etc. 
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d9bd25cd09f2de39b07b2584c69cba1751d42997efb5fcf3955f42388b083faa.png] Bilateral symmetry

 

 
• Radial Symmetry:

 
 
• For example Coelenterates, Echinoderms, and Ctenophores.
 
• Animals whose bodies can be** divided into two equal halves from any plane passing through the center of the body **are said to be radially symmetrical.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/837e5518146c767d9e994377211d886ee590f83ffe302dbe85d496a8261be2f9.png] Radial Symmetry

 
• 
 
 
• Asymmetrical:

 
 
• ​Few animals cannot be divided into two equivalent parts along with any plane going through the central point of the organism. They are said to be asymmetrical. 
 
• For example Sponges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **physical constant** known as **Boltzmann's constant** allows us to **calculate how much energy** is involved in the **random thermal movements** of the** constituent particles** of a substance.
 
• The **average kinetic energy of molecules** is** high **when the **temperature** of the gas molecules is** high,** according to **Austrian physicist Ludwig Boltzmann.**
 
• Temperature (R) ∝ Kinetic Energy (K.E.)
 
• The equation would be:
 
• **PV = N x Kb x T.**
 
• Here, P is the **Pressure** in Pascals, V is the **volume** in meter cubes, N = **No of molecules **of the gas, T = **Temperature**, and Kb is **Boltzmann’s constant.**
 
• S.I. unit of Kb =** Joule per kelvin.**
 
• The value of Boltzmann’s constant Kb in CGS is given by** 1.3806542×10−16 erg / Kelvin**.
 
• Dimensional formula of Boltzmann’s constant** :ML²T⁻²Θ⁻¹.**
 
• Boltzmann’s constant in electron Volt (eV) is equal to **0.000086173324 eV/ kelvin.**

questions.question: In 1785, who used the calibrated torsion balance to measure the force between electric charges?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Charles Augustin Coulomb**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Charles Augustin Coulomb French physicist** started his career as a **military engineer in the west indies**.
 
• **In 1785, he invented a torsional balance **and used it to perform experiments to determine the nature of interaction forces between charges and magnets.
 
• He presented the results of these experiments in the form of **Coulomb's law of electrostatics and Coulomb's law of magnetostatics**.
 
• The **SI unit of charge** has been named in the honor of Charles Augustin de Coulomb.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which odourless, colourless, tasteless and chemically unreactive gas was invented by Daniel Rutherford in 1772 and was independently isolated at the same time by CW Scheele and H Cavendish?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Nitrogen**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Discovered by** Daniel Rutherford in 1772,** nitrogen is a colorless, odorless, tasteless, and chemically unreactive gas.
 
• Although **Daniel Rutherford** is credited with the** discovery of nitrogen**, it's important to acknowledge that **Carl Wilhelm Scheele and Henry Cavendish** independently isolated the gas around the same time.
 
• However, their work did not fully recognize nitrogen as it was understood in Rutherford's research. Rutherford's identification of nitrogen occurred during his investigation into the composition of air.
 
• By** eliminating oxygen and carbon dioxide** from air, he isolated a gas that did not support combustion or sustain animal life, a gas now recognized as nitrogen.
 
• Constituting approximately 78% of the Earth's atmosphere by volume, nitrogen stands as the most abundant gas in the atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Argon, classified as a chemical element in the eighteenth group of the periodic table, is a noble gas and ranks as the third most abundant gas in the Earth's atmosphere.
 
• **Fluorine**, denoted by the symbol F and atomic number 9, is a chemical element.
 
• **Oxygen,** represented by the symbol O and atomic number 8, is a chemical element categorized as a nonmetal. Serving as an oxidizing agent, oxygen is highly reactive and exists as a colorless, odorless, and tasteless gas.

questions.question: What is the valency of Boron?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **number of atoms** of one element coupled with **one atom of another** to create a **molecule** is known as **valency.**
 
• **Valency and molecular weight** are two related terms.
 
• The** quantity of electrons **in an** element's outermost shell **determines its valency.
 
• **Valence electrons **are the electrons that make up the** outermost shell surrounding an atomic nucleus.**
 
• The **nucleus **of an atom is composed of **protons and neutrons. **
 
• **Electrons **revolve around the nucleus in a fixed path called **orbits or shells.**
 
• The names of the shells are** "K," "L," "M," "N," **and so forth.
 
• The **'K' shel**l, which may hold up to **2 electrons**, is the innermost shell.
 
• The **"L" shell**, which has up to **8 electrons**, comes next.
 
• The** "M" shell, **which has up to **18 electrons**, comes next.
 
• Up to** 32 electrons** can be found in the last **"N" shell.**​
 
• **Boron:**
 
 
• The atomic number of boron is **5.**
 
• There are** fewer than five electrons—three**—in the outer shell.
 
• It needs to provide or release these **electrons to stay stable.**
 
• **Two electrons **are located in the** K shell **and three are located in the** L shell **in accordance with the** octet rule.**
 
• It'll lose **three electrons.**
 
• The result is that boron has a **valency of 3.**​
 
 

2f

questions.question: Which of the following is the IUPAC name of m-Dichlorobenzene?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1,3-Dichlorobenzene**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **1,3-Dichlorobenzene** is the IUPAC name for m-Dichlorobenzene.
 
• The prefix "m-" stands for "meta-", indicating that the two chlorine atoms are positioned at the 1 and 3 positions on the benzene ring.
 
• This nomenclature follows the IUPAC rules for naming disubstituted benzene compounds, where the positions of the substituents are indicated by numbers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ortho-** (o-), **meta-** (m-), and **para-** (p-) are terms used to describe the relative positions of substituents on a benzene ring.
 
• In the **ortho-** position, substituents are adjacent (1,2-); in the **meta-** position, they are separated by one carbon (1,3-); and in the **para-** position, they are opposite each other (1,4-).
 
• Understanding these positions is crucial for proper chemical nomenclature and communication in organic chemistry.

questions.question: Which protein is found in grains?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gluten**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gluten** is the main protein found in grains such as wheat, barley, and rye.
 
• It is a composite of storage proteins, namely gliadin and glutenin, which are conjoined with starch in the endosperm of various grass-related grains.
 
• Gluten gives dough its elasticity, helping it rise and keep its shape, and often gives the final product a chewy texture.
 
• While it is a common ingredient in many foods, some individuals have gluten intolerance or celiac disease, which requires them to follow a gluten-free diet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Celiac disease** is an autoimmune disorder where ingestion of gluten leads to damage in the small intestine.
 
• A **gluten-free diet** involves excluding foods that contain gluten, which is found in wheat, barley, rye, and derivatives of these grains.
 
• Gluten-free products are widely available and are essential for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.
 
• Despite its necessity for some, a gluten-free diet is also adopted by others for various health benefits or lifestyle choices.
